key_insight: A deep-learning–reconstructed accelerated whole-body DWI protocol cut scan time by 37% while preserving image quality and ADC measurements in metastatic prostate cancer.
clinical_relevance: If validated more broadly, this approach could make prostate cancer staging and response assessment faster without sacrificing quantitative imaging reliability.
method: Prospective single-centre study at 1.5T with two patient cohorts
Compared standard WB-DWI vs accelerated DL-reconstructed WB-DWI
Assessed radiologist image quality and lesion ADC agreement
evidence_signal: Radiologists rated both protocols as good-to-excellent, and lesion ADC estimates showed no significant difference between standard and accelerated scans.
watch_item: Results come from a small, single-centre study, so broader multi-site validation is still needed before routine adoption.
paper_title: Evaluation of accelerated whole-body diffusion weighted imaging with deep learning reconstruction in patients with metastatic prostate cancer: assessment of image quality and ADC estimates.
